newsitem.title: BELGIUM: EU olive oil subsidy reform plans set for delay.
newsitem.headline: EU olive oil subsidy reform plans set for delay.

text.p: European Union plans to simplify olive oil subsidies and combat rampant fraud are likely to be delayed until at least the autumn due to strong opposition from producer countries, EU officials and diplomats said on Friday.
Spain, backed by Portugal, Greece and Italy, is expected to strongly attack a reform linking subsidies to the number of productive trees at a meeting of EU farm ministers on Tuesday.
The producers prefer an alternative that would retain the production-based subsidy system but would scrap special aid for small producers, seen as the main source of fraud.
Spain said a tree-based system would discourage efforts to improve yields and quality and would throw tens of thousands of rural workers out of work.
"Everyone agrees on the need to fight fraud but they differ sharply on how to do it," said one diplomat, adding that reform proposals were unlikely until late this year.
Both options for reform were presented by the European Commission in a report in February which noted that olive oil fraud was proportionately 10 times greater than for cereals and other crops.
Fraud is rampant because of the difficulty of controlling the large number of small olive oil producers and preventing them from abusing the aid system.
Diplomats said there was also deep disagreement over olive oil market trends.
The EU's executive commission, supported by consumers, forecast a growing surplus as a result of increasing production and stagnant consumption and exports.
Producers say the prediction is based on figures for the last two years which are unrepresentative and that greater effort should be made to boost consumption.
Officials added the EU's executive commission is waiting for the opinion of the European Parliament, expected in the autumn, before drafting reform proposals.
